claims.claim: Curtiss-Wright won an approximately $14M Northrop Grumman contract for sensor-processing equipment in the U.S. Army Improved Threat Detection System, exposing the company to open-architecture airborne threat-detection modernization.
Curtiss-Wright is investing $80M over multiple years to expand Cheswick operations serving naval defense and commercial nuclear demand, signaling capacity commitment to two long-duration end markets.

risks.risk: Program awards and capacity investments depend on government/nuclear schedules and can face timing or mix volatility.

unknowns.unknown: The ITDS award is small relative to company scale; follow-on production value is not established by the announcement.

claims.claim: Q2 2026 adjusted EPS grew 15%, adjusted operating margin expanded 110 bps to 19.4%, orders were $1.1B at 1.16x book-to-bill and backlog reached $4.5B; management raised full-year sales, operating income, margin, EPS and free-cash-flow guidance.
On September 10 the board raised total available repurchase authorization to $700M and expanded 2026 repurchases again, with expected 2026 repurchases of $460M.

risks.risk: Large repurchases reduce capital flexibility if end-market demand or acquisition opportunities change.

unknowns.unknown: Q3 operating results have not yet tested the raised Q2 guidance.
